mechanism: The handler (src/rpc/mining.lisp:1005-1038) validates fee_delta with INTEGERP only, and yason parses a JSON integer literal of any magnitude into a bignum, so an out-of-int64 delta reaches MEMPOOL-PRIORITISE unchecked. MEMPOOL-PRIORITISE (src/mempool/mempool.lisp:262-281) then mutates in the wrong order: it does (INCF (MEMPOOL-ENTRY-MODIFIED-FEE ENTRY) FEE-DELTA) FIRST and only afterwards calls TXGRAPH-SET-TRANSACTION-FEE, whose (SETF (FEEFRAC-FEE ...)) hits the (SIGNED-BYTE 64) slot declaration at src/mempool/feefrac.lisp:22 and signals a raw SIMPLE-TYPE-ERROR; the MEMPOOL-DELTAS table update and %MEMPOOL-GRAPH-VERIFY both sit after the failing call, so neither runs. Core reads the delta as CAmount nAmount = request.params[2].getInt<int64_t>() at refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/mining.cpp:526, i.e. UniValue range-checks and throws BEFORE any state is touched, and its PrioritiseTransaction updates mapDeltas and the entry together under pool.cs. The same shape is reachable with an in-range delta whose SUM with the existing modified fee crosses int64.
consequence: One RPC call permanently desynchronises the mempool entry from the txgraph, and the entry can never be repaired through the RPC that broke it. Executed through the shipped dispatcher with yason-parsed params: the call raised (:RAW-ERROR TYPE-ERROR "The value 1180591620717411313424 is not of type (SIGNED-BYTE 64) when setting slot FEE of structure FEEFRAC") -- the JSON-RPC server converts a non-rpc-error into +rpc-internal-error+ (src/rpc/server.lisp:415-417), so the operator gets an internal error rather than Core's clean parameter error -- and left (:ENTRY-MODIFIED-FEE 1180591620717411313424 :GRAPH-FEE 10000 :DELTAS-COUNT 0). Three consequences, all executed. The delta is invisible and unrecoverable: getprioritisedtransactions returned an empty table, and with MEMPOOL-DELTAS empty a mempool.dat round trip drops it. The entry is permanently unprioritisable: a SECOND, perfectly well-formed call with fee_delta 100 also type-errored and pushed the entry's modified fee further out, to 1180591620717411313524. And the split is load-bearing in opposite directions -- %RBF-REPLACED-FEES reads the ENTRY's modified fee, so rule 3 now demands ~1.18e21 satoshis and a replacement that succeeded before the corrupting call (check-rbf-rules -> T) is refused afterwards with :INSUFFICIENT-FEE, while eviction and mining read the GRAPH (mempool-trim-to-size takes txgraph-get-worst-main-chunk, src/mempool/mempool.lisp:1736-1755) and still see fee 10000 over size 95, so the transaction is evictable at its original feerate while claiming an astronomical one. Operator-triggered over the RPC, not remote, and it costs no funds -- which is what holds it at S2 (a permanent split of two data structures) rather than S1.
evidence: Probes under build/ga11v/p6-prioritise.lisp, run with scripts/dev.sh eval on the project container in worktree bl-ga11v-storage-s2, with bl.mp:*txgraph-shadow-checks* bound to NIL. Params are built the way a real request arrives: (yason:parse "[<txid>, 0, 1180591620717411303424]") through bl.rpc::%normalize-rpc-params, then bl.rpc:dispatch-rpc-method. (1) ga11v-p6 -> (:BEFORE (:ENTRY-MODIFIED-FEE 10000 :GRAPH-FEE 10000 :DELTAS-COUNT 0) :FIRST-CALL (:RAW-ERROR TYPE-ERROR ...) :AFTER-FIRST (:ENTRY-MODIFIED-FEE 1180591620717411313424 :GRAPH-FEE 10000 :DELTAS-COUNT 0) :SECOND-CALL (:RAW-ERROR TYPE-ERROR) :AFTER-SECOND (:ENTRY-MODIFIED-FEE 1180591620717411313524 :GRAPH-FEE 10000 :DELTAS-COUNT 0) :GETPRIORITISEDTRANSACTIONS <empty hash-table> :RULE3-REPLACED-FEES 1180591620717411313524 :GRAPH-AND-ENTRY-AGREE NIL). (2) ga11v-p6-effects, the replacement/eviction half with a before/after control on the same fixture -> (:RBF-BEFORE (T NIL) :RBF-AFTER (NIL :INSUFFICIENT-FEE) :ENTRY-MODIFIED-FEE 1180591620717411313424 :GRAPH-MAIN-CHUNK-FEE 10000 :GRAPH-MAIN-CHUNK-SIZE 95). Ours: src/rpc/mining.lisp:1005-1038; src/mempool/mempool.lisp:262-281,1188-1208,1229-1276,1736-1755; src/mempool/feefrac.lisp:19-23; src/rpc/server.lisp:415-417. Core at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/rpc/mining.cpp:520-535; refs/bitcoin/src/txmempool.cpp PrioritiseTransaction.
fix_shape: Do not implement here. Range-check before touching state, which is exactly what Core's getInt<int64_t> does, and then make the two writes atomic. In the handler, replace the bare INTEGERP test with a typep against (signed-byte 64) and raise the same -8 rpc-error text Core's UniValue throw produces, so an out-of-range fee_delta never reaches the mempool. That alone is not sufficient, because an in-range delta can still overflow when summed with the entry's existing modified fee: MEMPOOL-PRIORITISE should compute the new modified fee and the new accumulated delta FIRST, check both against (signed-byte 64), and only then write the entry, the txgraph and MEMPOOL-DELTAS -- signalling an rpc-error and leaving all three untouched if either would overflow, which matches Core's ordering where mapDeltas and the entry move together under pool.cs. Worth doing in the same change: the three writes in MEMPOOL-PRIORITISE are the only place the entry's modified fee and the txgraph's fee are supposed to move in lockstep, so a %MEMPOOL-GRAPH-VERIFY (or an explicit assertion that the two agree) belongs on the success path where it cannot be skipped by an escaping condition. A test should drive both the out-of-range literal and the summed-overflow case through dispatch-rpc-method and assert an rpc-error plus unchanged entry fee, graph fee and deltas count, with the positive control that an ordinary in-range delta still moves all three.
